questions.q: Which landform is formed by DEPOSITION?
questions.why: A spit is a ridge of sand or shingle deposited by longshore drift.

questions.q: What is the correct order of landforms from a crack in a headland?
questions.why: A crack becomes a cave, then an arch, then a stack, then a stump.

questions.q: In longshore drift, backwash carries material
options: at an angle along the beach
straight down the beach at right angles to the coast
away from the shore in suspension
questions.why: Gravity pulls backwash straight down the slope; swash moves up at an angle, creating a zigzag.

questions.q: Explain how a cave, arch and stack form.
questions.model: Hydraulic action and abrasion enlarge a crack in a headland to form a cave. The cave erodes through the headland, forming an arch. The arch is weakened by erosion and weathering and its roof collapses, leaving a stack.
points: cave forms from crack by hydraulic action/abrasion; erodes through headland to arch
arch roof collapses leaving a stack
